initial_gap: The local gate lock ended after sandbox execution but before output inventory and durable receipt publication; gated attempt-1 stages did not retain release-claim provenance.

local_contract.gated_stage_schema: new gated stages use schema 2 from attempt 1; unsequenced and historical schema-1 stages remain readable but do not retain a gate
local_contract.lock_scope: shared gate lock is acquired before admission claim and durable call reservation and held through sandbox, output inventory, post-run checks and receipt file and directory fsync
local_contract.registry_paths: gate, admission, release, stage, receipt and session destinations are checked to keep registry roots disjoint and gate state free of application outputs
local_contract.scope: cooperating processes with the same UID, host and private registry roots

adversarial_reproductions_and_repairs: A terminal writer paused behind the gate lock while one-shot receipt publication was paused for attempts 1 and 2; it completed only after the receipt was durable.
A terminal writer paused while a session terminal receipt was already fsynced but the call still held the gate; it completed after the session released the lock.
Closing the gate between point-in-time verification and lock acquisition now rejects a call without publishing an admission claim or reservation.
One-shot receipt and session destinations inside the gate previously poisoned its strict state directory; guarded paths now reject them before mutation.
Identical or nested gate and admission roots previously caused a shared-to-exclusive self-deadlock; path and existing-inode checks reject this configuration before the gate lock.
Release and stage destinations inside the gate are rejected before a claim or output directory is created.
A concurrent admission loser may fail closed because the registry directory changed during the operation; its test accepts this safe rejection while still requiring no losing reservation.

gates.command: .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/test_local_block_release_gate.py tests/test_preflight_assets.py tests/test_stage_released_run.py tests/test_verify_staged_run.py tests/test_local_run_admission.py tests/test_run_staged_local_tool.py tests/test_staged_tool_session.py
ruff check scripts tests; git diff --check

independent_review.result: The reviewer reproduced a spent-reservation race, registry self-poisoning and a shared-to-exclusive self-deadlock; final scoped re-review found no further reproducible issue in the supported gated path model.
independent_review.remaining_explicit_bypass: An attempt-1 release has schema 1 and can be re-staged with development_unsequenced; that explicit development mode is outside gate sequencing.
independent_review.remaining_local_threat: A hostile process with the same UID can mutate paths or registries; these cooperative checks do not establish independent custody.

limits: The operator's terminal and its incident, trace and artifact digests remain local declarations, without authenticated provider evidence.
A legacy schema-1 stage does not record its gate and cannot retroactively retain it during execution.
These synthetic local tool tests do not execute the model matrix, validate a provider's runtime image or enforce global token, time and cost limits.
The unrelated MCP same-UID relocation counterexample remains the one strict expected failure in the global suite.
